text:
The new Valkey server (port 6380) now holds an exact copy of all the data, but I caused an outage on the Redis server partway through. You need to know about that first.

**The incident:** a script I wrote to inspect the data had a bug that made it loop forever. Memory filled up and the system killed the Redis 8.10 server (port 6379) at about 06:52. I restarted it with its normal config file. It reloaded its last on-disk snapshot, taken automatically at 06:49:43, which has the same 3310 keys it held before the crash. It was down for about 2 minutes. No clients were connected afterwards and the data looks unchanged. But if anything wrote to it between 06:49:43 and the crash, those writes are lost. Please check your application logs for that window. I saved a copy of the snapshot at `/root/backup/redis-old-dump-1791010466.rdb`.

**How the data was copied:** Valkey can't load Redis 8's data files or replicate from it (its migration docs say this for Redis 7.4 and later). So I wrote a script, `/tmp/migrate.py`, that reads every key from Redis and rebuilds it on Valkey with ordinary commands. It only reads from Redis and never writes to it.
- **Expiry times:** key and hash-field expiries are copied as exact end times, not remaining seconds, so they match exactly.
- **Streams:** entries keep their original IDs, along with the stream's internal counters. Consumer groups are recreated with the same read position, consumers and pending messages, including each message's delivery time and retry count.

**Check:** a second script, `/tmp/verify.py`, compared all 3310 keys (2960 in db0, 350 in db2) on both servers. It checked type, value, expiry times and the full stream group state, and found 0 differences.

**Things that don't carry over exactly:**
- The "last seen" and "last active" times of stream consumers show the time of the copy, because Valkey has no command to set them.
- Redis 8's idempotent-producer tracking for streams isn't copied, because Valkey doesn't have that feature. Nothing was being tracked, so no data is affected.

**Current state:**
- **Valkey:** runs as a standalone primary with no replication settings. It accepted a test write, which I then deleted. I saved its data to disk.
- **Redis:** running with its data unchanged.
